title: Socks in the dark
prompt:
A drawer holds 12 loose socks: 6 red, 4 blue and 2 green. The room is completely dark, so you can't see colours. You take socks out one at a time and don't put any back.

What is the smallest number of socks you must take to be **certain** of having at least two blue socks?
hints: Being certain means planning for the unluckiest possible draws. What would the unluckiest draws be?
How many socks could you take without getting a single blue one?
After all of those, how many more draws could still give you only one blue sock?
solution:
**10 socks.**

Plan for the worst luck. You could draw all 6 red and both green socks first, which is 8 socks and no blue. The 9th sock must be blue, but one blue sock isn't a pair. The 10th sock must also be blue, because only blue socks are left.

With 9 socks you could still have just one blue, so 9 is not enough. 10 always works.
